back: A change in the ownership, control or use of land to make its distribution more equal or more productive.

front: Why did land reform take place in Zimbabwe?
back: Unequal land distribution at independence, overcrowded communal areas, expectations after the liberation struggle, and slow early resettlement.
Land Apportionment Act (1930) and Land Tenure Act (1969) reserved the better land mainly for white commercial farmers.
For the first ten years land acquisition had to be on a willing buyer, willing seller basis.
Small plots for household farming, either villagised (clustered homes, shared grazing) or self-contained (house and fields on one farm).
Larger plots for small to medium commercial farming, with dispersed homesteads.
New settlements and higher density on former farms; services lagged; new business centres; changes for farm workers.

front: Why does a villagised layout help service provision?
back: Clustered households share a school, clinic or borehole and reduce the cost per household.
Farmers invest in buildings and equipment and can borrow money if they are sure of their land rights.
